items.stem: Why do places east of Greenwich have time ahead of GMT?
items.answer: The earth rotates from west to east, so places to the east see the sun earlier; 1° = 4 minutes.

items.stem: The local time at a place X at 70° E is 7:00 a.m.. Calculate the local time at a place Y at 20° E. Show your working.
items.answer: Difference in longitude = 50°; time difference = 50 × 4 = 200 minutes (3 hours 20 minutes). Y lies to the west of X, so its time is behind: 7:00 a.m. − 3 hours 20 minutes = 3:40 a.m..
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for difference in longitude (50°), 1 for time difference (3 hours 20 minutes at 4 minutes per degree), 1 for subtracting because Y is to the west (3:40 a.m.).

"There are 360 meridians at an interval of 1°, 180 to the east and 180 to the west of the Prime Meridian. The latitude and longitude of a place together give its exact location. Parallels of latitude decrease in size from the equator towards the poles."
(i) The network of parallels and meridians is called: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'Prime Meridian' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Latitude and longitude are both needed to locate a place. (1)
items.answer: (i) graticule (ii) The meridian of 0° longitude that passes through Greenwich near London. (iii) Latitude alone gives only a parallel and longitude alone gives only a meridian.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) graticule (ii) The meridian of 0° longitude that passes through Greenwich near London. (iii) Latitude alone gives only a parallel and longitude alone gives only a meridian.

items.stem: The International Date Line is zigzag because it:
items.answer: avoids land areas and island groups
items.markingKey: (c) avoids land areas and island groups.
options: avoids land areas and island groups

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about parallels of latitude and meridians of longitude:
I. All parallels are of equal length.
II. The equator passes through Greenwich.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Neither I nor II
items.markingKey: (d) I is incorrect: Parallels decrease in size from the equator to the poles; meridians are equal. II is incorrect: The Prime Meridian passes through Greenwich; the equator is 0° latitude.

items.stem: "The distance covered by one degree of longitude decreases towards the poles." Examine this statement with reference to parallels of latitude and meridians of longitude.
items.answer: The statement is valid. All meridians converge and meet at the poles.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (all meridians converge and meet at the poles.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem: In the study of standard time, time zones and the International Date Line, the term 'time zone' refers to:
items.answer: A region of the earth that observes the same standard time, generally 15° of longitude wide
items.markingKey: (b) 'time zone' means a region of the earth that observes the same standard time, generally 15° of longitude wide.
options: A semi-circle joining the poles that connects places of the same longitude
A region of the earth that observes the same standard time, generally 15° of longitude wide
The network of parallels and meridians drawn on a globe or map
A circle joining places of the same latitude, parallel to the equator

items.stem: What is the difference in local time between two places located at 80° W and 105° W?
items.answer: 1 hour 40 minutes
items.markingKey: (b) Difference in longitude = 25°; time = 25 × 4 minutes = 100 minutes = 1 hour 40 minutes.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about longitude and time: calculating local time:
I. The earth rotates from east to west.
II. A difference of 1° of longitude gives a difference of 4 minutes in local time.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: II only
items.markingKey: (b) I is incorrect: It rotates from west to east. II is correct.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on standard time, time zones and the International Date Line and answer the questions that follow.
"Standard time avoids the confusion of different local times within a country. The time at 180° east and 180° west is the same, but the date differs by a day. The International Date Line deviates from the 180° meridian to avoid dividing land areas."
(i) The world is divided into how many time zones of one hour each? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'standard time' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Countries adopt a standard time. (1)
items.answer: (i) 24 (ii) The local time of a central meridian adopted for the whole of a country or time zone. (iii) Local times differ from place to place, and a single time avoids confusion in railways, offices and communication.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) 24 (ii) The local time of a central meridian adopted for the whole of a country or time zone. (iii) Local times differ from place to place, and a single time avoids confusion in railways, offices and communication.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The earth rotates through 1° in 15 minutes.
Reason (R): The earth turns through 360° in 24 hours, that is 1° every 4 minutes.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: It rotates through 1° in 4 minutes and 15° in one hour. R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about standard time, time zones and the International Date Line:
I. Some large countries with a wide east-west extent have more than one time zone.
II. The time at 180° east and 180° west is the same, but the date differs by a day.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Both I and II
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): All parallels are of equal length.
Reason (R): All meridians converge and meet at the poles.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Parallels decrease in size from the equator to the poles; meridians are equal. R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which term describes the following? The local time of the Prime Meridian (0°) at Greenwich, used as the world reference time.
items.answer: Greenwich Mean Time
items.markingKey: (c) Greenwich Mean Time: the local time of the Prime Meridian (0°) at Greenwich, used as the world reference time.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about parallels of latitude and meridians of longitude is correct?
items.answer: The distance between two meridians decreases from the equator towards the poles.
items.markingKey: (b) The others are wrong: Parallels decrease in size from the equator to the poles; meridians are equal. It is greatest at the equator and decreases to zero at the poles. The Prime Meridian passes through Greenwich; the equator is 0° latitude.
options: The distance between meridians is the same everywhere.
The distance between two meridians decreases from the equator towards the poles.
All parallels are of equal length.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on longitude and time: calculating local time and answer the questions that follow.
"A difference of 1° of longitude gives a difference of 4 minutes in local time. Local time is based on the time when the sun is highest in the sky at a place. The earth rotates from west to east, through 360° in 24 hours."
(i) The earth rotates through 15° of longitude in: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'local time' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: There is a four-minute difference in local time for every degree of longitude. (1)
items.answer: (i) 1 hour (ii) The time of a place determined by the position of the sun, when the sun is overhead at noon on its meridian. (iii) The earth turns through 360° in 24 hours, that is 1° every 4 minutes.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) 1 hour (ii) The time of a place determined by the position of the sun, when the sun is overhead at noon on its meridian. (iii) The earth turns through 360° in 24 hours, that is 1° every 4 minutes.

items.stem:
Statement: The International Date Line is not a straight line.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: It bends to avoid dividing countries and island groups into two dates.
items.markingKey: (b) It bends to avoid dividing countries and island groups into two dates.
options: Local times differ from place to place, and a single time avoids confusion in railways, offices and communication.
It bends to avoid dividing countries and island groups into two dates.
They have a large east-west extent, so one standard time would differ too much from local times.
It lies midway between the poles where the earth is widest.

items.stem: In the study of parallels of latitude and meridians of longitude, the term 'parallel of latitude' refers to:
items.answer: A circle joining places of the same latitude, parallel to the equator
items.markingKey: (c) 'parallel of latitude' means a circle joining places of the same latitude, parallel to the equator.
options: The local time of the Prime Meridian (0°) at Greenwich, used as the world reference time
The line roughly along 180° longitude, where the date changes by one day on crossing it
A circle joining places of the same latitude, parallel to the equator
The local time of a central meridian adopted for the whole of a country or time zone

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about standard time, time zones and the International Date Line is correct?
items.answer: Indian Standard Time is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich Mean Time.
items.markingKey: (d) The others are wrong: He gains a day (the date advances); crossing west to east, he repeats a day. Countries adopt standard time based on a central meridian. It roughly follows the 180° meridian.
options: Crossing the Date Line from east to west, a traveller repeats a day.
The International Date Line follows the 0° meridian.
Every country uses its own local time for each city.
Indian Standard Time is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich Mean Time.

items.stem:
Statement: Places to the east of Greenwich are ahead of GMT.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: The earth rotates from west to east, so the sun rises earlier there.
items.markingKey: (d) The earth rotates from west to east, so the sun rises earlier there.
options: They have a large east-west extent, so one standard time would differ too much from local times.
It bends to avoid dividing countries and island groups into two dates.
The earth turns through 360° in 24 hours, that is 1° every 4 minutes.
The earth rotates from west to east, so the sun rises earlier there.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about longitude and time: calculating local time is correct?
items.answer: Places east of a meridian are ahead in time, and places west are behind.
items.markingKey: (d) The others are wrong: It rotates through 1° in 4 minutes and 15° in one hour. It rotates from west to east. They are behind GMT; places to the east are ahead.
options: The earth rotates through 1° in 15 minutes.
Places to the west of Greenwich are ahead of GMT.
The earth rotates from east to west.
Places east of a meridian are ahead in time, and places west are behind.

items.stem: The following statement about parallels of latitude and meridians of longitude is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "The equator passes through Greenwich."
items.answer: The Prime Meridian passes through Greenwich; the equator is 0° latitude.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (The Prime Meridian passes through Greenwich; the equator is 0° latitude.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on parallels of latitude and meridians of longitude and answer the questions that follow.
"There are 360 meridians at an interval of 1°, 180 to the east and 180 to the west of the Prime Meridian. The latitude and longitude of a place together give its exact location. The distance between two meridians decreases from the equator towards the poles."
(i) The latitude of the Arctic Circle is: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'longitude' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Latitude and longitude are both needed to locate a place. (1)
items.answer: (i) 66½° N (ii) The angular distance of a place east or west of the Prime Meridian, measured in degrees. (iii) Latitude alone gives only a parallel and longitude alone gives only a meridian.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) 66½° N (ii) The angular distance of a place east or west of the Prime Meridian, measured in degrees. (iii) Latitude alone gives only a parallel and longitude alone gives only a meridian.
